Lemma
[Anisotropic heat uniqueness on bounded cylinders] \group Maximum Principles ↗ lem:weak-maximum-principle-heat-anisotropic

Let $U \subset \R ^n$ be open, bounded and nonempty, and let $T>0$. If two continuous functions on $\overline{U_T}$ have one time derivative and two pure spatial derivatives on every coordinate line at interior times, solve the same heat equation with source $f$ there, and agree on the parabolic boundary, then they agree on $\overline{U_T}$. This is the bounded-domain uniqueness argument under Evans's $C^2_1$-style line regularity: subtract the solutions, observe that the source cancels, and apply the anisotropic weak maximum principle to the difference and its negative.
Proof

The line derivatives are stable under subtraction, and the common source cancels in the line-form heat equations. The anisotropic weak maximum principle bounds the difference above by its parabolic-boundary value, while the same argument for the negative difference bounds it below. Boundary agreement therefore gives equality throughout the closed cylinder.

□
